strategy.viewer: Curious adult who has tried holding their breath and wondered why it burns, and who likes human-body limits (series: Your Body at the Limit).
strategy.hook: The burning in your chest is not your body running out of oxygen.
strategy.promise: Title and thumbnail promise: the real trigger of the urge to breathe, which is not oxygen, and how long humans can actually go.
strategy.payoff: Most people last about a minute; the limit is a carbon-dioxide alarm, not an oxygen shortage; trained freedivers wait it out for about eleven and a half to twelve minutes (about 24 with pure oxygen); and hyperventilating mutes the alarm and causes blackouts.
strategy.takeaway: Your urge to breathe is a smoke detector, not a fuel gauge.

scenes.text: A freediver once held his breath for more than twenty-four minutes.
Croatia, 2021: a Guinness World Record, set after breathing pure oxygen to load his body with reserve.
On plain air, the record is about eleven and a half to twelve minutes.
What stops the rest of us is not oxygen. It is carbon dioxide, setting off an alarm in your brain.
Please never try this in water. The full story is on the channel. Subscribe for the next one.

youtube.title: Your Urge to Breathe Is Not What You Think

titles: Your Urge to Breathe Is Not What You Think
How Long Can You Really Hold Your Breath?
Why You Can't Hold Your Breath Longer

youtube.description:
Why can't you hold your breath for longer? Because the burning urge to breathe is not about oxygen. It is about carbon dioxide, and a freediver learns to wait that alarm out for almost twelve minutes. We follow the alarm from your brainstem to your diaphragm, meet seals, whales and the dive reflex, and explain the deadly trap of shallow water blackout.

In this video:
- The burning feeling
- The wrong alarm
- The built-in diving machine
- The trap that kills

SAFETY: never hold your breath in or near water alone, never hyperventilate before swimming underwater, and never push through the alarm in a pool, lake or sea. Do not attempt records. This video is education, not training advice.

FAQ
How long can a person hold their breath? Most untrained people last about a minute.
Why do you have to breathe? Rising carbon dioxide, not falling oxygen, triggers the urge.
What is the record? About 11.5-12 minutes on plain air and over 24 minutes after breathing pure oxygen (Guinness).
What is the mammalian dive reflex? Cold water on the face slows the heart and reroutes blood to heart and brain.
What is shallow water blackout? Loss of consciousness from low oxygen, often after hyperventilating, with no warning.
